summary: A strong paper: everyday booking call, a social-setting talk with a well-built matching box, a two-student discussion full of rejected options, and an 826-word lecture. All keys are correct; one explanation named the wrong speaker and is fixed.
strengths: Part 1 has textbook distractors: birthday rejected for anniversary, the 7th taken so the 14th, fifty corrected to sixty, the weekday rate printed and the weekend rate tested.
Part 2 MCQs name both wrong options first as things people assume (Q11, Q13, Q14), and the matching box includes a deliberate trap ("brand new" play area vs "just been rebuilt" chicken house).
Part 3 multi-selects require listening to which problems are dismissed (noise, word list, session length) and which changes are refused (quieter room, reward, shorter questionnaire).
Part 4 gives a full lecture with dates, a misleading "first market" (cars vs bicycles) and paraphrased note headings.

issues.problem: The explanation said Nilufar lists the two serious problems; in the script Karim names them and Nilufar agrees.
The old paraphrase pair used "returned after the event", which is not in the table the student reads; Q7 has no real paraphrase (the table says "Deposit (refundable)").
Q18 option "has just been rebuilt" is heard word for word ("it has just been rebuilt").
issues.change: Reword the option, e.g. "has been replaced after an attack".

issues.problem: A few Part 4 notes echo the lecture exactly ("heated rubber together with {{35}}", "the milky {{31}} of a tropical tree").
issues.change: Reword, e.g. "1839: Goodyear combined rubber and {{35}} under heat".
